title: fix(git.repo.test): --resnap with a name:// scope deletes every sibling snapshot in the file
description:
## .what
git.repo.test --resnap combined with a --scope name://X deletes every snapshot in the file whose test the name filter skipped. --scope name:// maps to jest --testNamePattern and --resnap maps to -u; under -u, jest treats each snapshot whose test did not run as obsolete and removes it. the run exits 0 and prints naught about the loss.

evidence: a run scoped to one integration test file with --scope name://case16 --resnap --mode apply passed, and the .snap file lost every key outside case16. it was caught only because a git diff showed a wholesale deletion; a whole-file --resnap restored them.

## .why
- the skill help recommends the narrow path:// plus name:// stack as the fastest loop, and recommends --resnap to update snapshots. the two recommended moves compose into silent data loss
- a driver who does not diff the .snap ships a suite that lost coverage, and a reviewer reads the deletion as intentional

## .shape of the fix
- refuse --resnap beside any name:// scope, exit 2, and print the fix: drop the name scope, keep the path scope (a whole-file resnap)
- clamp: a temp repo with one test file of two snapshotted cases; run with --scope name://case1 --resnap; assert the refusal, and that the case2 key survives
